sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two aspects of dwelling in the sukkah by Israel's own power, distinguishing between the command "Basukkot Teishvei" and the narrative "Yeishvu Basukkot," which correspond to the near and far encompassing lights, with the latter relating to the essence of the soul rooted in Atzmus.

translations.translation: Now, also regarding the dwelling in the sukkah of Israel by their own power,
there are two matters.
"Basukkot Teishvei" etc.,
and "Kol HaEzrach B'Yisrael Yeishvu Basukkot."
And among the distinctions between these two matters,
"Basukkot Teishvei" is in the language of a command,
while "Yeishvu Basukkot" is in the language of narrative and announcement.
And another distinction,
that the command "Basukkot Teishvei" is for all of Israel,
whereas those who "Yeishvu Basukkot"
(by themselves,
and do not need a command for this)
are
(only)
"the native-born in Israel."
And it is explained in the maamar,
that in the encompassing lights there are two levels,
the near encompassing light and the far encompassing light.
And these two matters of "Basukkot Teishvei" and "Yeishvu Basukkot" are in these two levels.
"Basukkot Teishvei" is in the near encompassing light, and "Yeishvu Basukkot" is in the far encompassing light.
And this is why regarding "Yeishvu Basukkot" it says "Kol HaEzrach B'Yisrael,"
for "Ezrach B'Yisrael" is the essence of the soul that is rooted in the Awtsmoos,
and the dwelling in the far encompassing light is on the level of the essence of the soul.
And it can be said,
that this is why "Yeishvu Basukkot" is not in the language of a command but in the language of narrative and announcement,
for the matter of command applies only to the level of the soul that is clothed in the body,
but regarding the soul above,
and especially regarding the essence of the soul,
there is no command.
And the matter of "Yeishvu Basukkot,"
that the essence of the soul dwells in the far encompassing light,
is
(not because of the command,
but)
from its own essence,
because its root is in the Awtsmoos.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "Kol HaEzrach B'Yisrael Yeishvu Basukkot" serves as the reason for "Basukkot Teishvei," raising the question of why this additional reason is needed beyond the explicit verse "Ki Basukkot Hoshavti."

translations.translation: And it is explained in the maamar,
that "Kol HaEzrach B'Yisrael Yeishvu Basukkot" is a reason for "Basukkot Teishvei."
That is, the power for "Basukkot Teishvei,"
to draw down the near encompassing light,
is because the essence of the soul
(the "Ezrach B'Yisrael")
is rooted in the Awtsmoos
(the far encompassing light).
And it needs to be understood,
that the reason
(and the power)
for "Basukkot Teishvei" is
(as is explicit in the verse)
"Ki Basukkot Hoshavti,"
so why is the reason of "Kol HaEzrach B'Yisrael Yeishvu Basukkot" also needed?

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the difficulty that since encompassing lights are inherently unsettled, Israel's dwelling in the sukkah causes a change in the lights themselves, raising the question of how human action can effect change in supernal lights.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing,
that since the encompassing lights
(as they are in themselves)
do not come into settlement,
therefore, that by Israel dwelling in the sukkah they are drawn into inwardness and settlement,
is like a change in the encompassing lights.
And moreover,
from the language of the maamar that by dwelling in the sukkah they draw the encompassing lights into inwardness and they become settled lights
(and not "they draw the encompassing lights into inwardness and settlement")
it implies,
that the change that occurs by Israel dwelling in the sukkah is also in the encompassing lights themselves.
For in addition to this, that by dwelling in the sukkah they are drawn into inwardness and settlement,
also the encompassing lights themselves are changed to become settled lights.
And it needs to be understood,
how is it possible that through the work of man
(dwelling in the sukkah)
there should be a change in the lights above.
